key_insight: A geometric invariant energy quadratization (IEQ) formulation enables curvature-driven surface evolution with unconditional discrete energy decay, independent of tangential motion.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports energy-stable finite element simulation of curvature-driven interface evolution, including anisotropic Willmore and H⁻¹-gradient flows.
method: Introduce a square-root auxiliary variable to express the geometric energy as a quadratic functional.
Use skew-symmetric surface transport so the energy law depends only on normal velocity.
Couple the IEQ discretization to monolithic nonlinear parametric FEM with BGN or minimal-deformation-rate tangential motion.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments demonstrating robustness and accuracy, but provides no quantitative errors or runtime comparisons.
watch_item: Unconditional energy decay does not eliminate nonlinear solver costs or time-step accuracy concerns; this is a numerical FEM method, not an AI surrogate.
paper_title: A geometric-IEQ approach for curvature-driven flows
